about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Fisherman's Pie
recipes.summary: Chunks of white fish, salmon and prawns in a parsley cream sauce under golden cheesy mash.
steps: Boil the potato for 18 minutes, until soft. Drain, mash with half the butter, a splash of milk and salt.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Soften the onion in the remaining butter for 5 minutes. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick.
Off the heat, fold in the fish, salmon, prawns, peas, parsley and lemon juice. Pour into a baking dish.
Spoon the mash on top, rough it up with a fork and scatter with the cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked through and the top is golden.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains fish, shellfish, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Cumberland Pie (Mince and Potato Pie with Cheesy Crumb Top)
recipes.summary: Savoury beef mince in rich gravy under mashed potato and a crisp cheese and breadcrumb topping.
steps: Boil the potato for 18 minutes, until soft. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and salt.
Brown the mince in a pan for 8 minutes, then add the onion and carrot and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour for 1 minute, add the stock and worcestershire, and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the mince into a dish, top with the mash, then the cheese mixed with the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 25 minutes, until bubbling and golden on top.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Scottish Bridies (Beef Pasties from Forfar)
recipes.summary: Half-moon shortcrust pasties filled with beef, onion and a little butter, a Scottish bakery classic.
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour with 1/2 tsp salt, then mix in about 1/2 cup ice water until it forms a dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, onion, suet, stock, pepper and 1 tsp salt.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roll out the dough and cut four 18cm rounds. Put the filling on one half, fold over and crimp the edge firmly.
Brush with egg, cut a small steam hole, and bake for 35 minutes, until golden and the filling is hot and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes before eating.
notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and egg. Cut one open to check the beef is hot all the way through.

recipes.title: Dublin Coddle
recipes.summary: Pork sausages and bacon gently simmered with potatoes and onions in a mild, savoury broth.
steps: Lightly brown the sausages and bacon in a heavy pot for 8 minutes. Remove and cut the sausages in thirds.
Layer the onion, potato, sausages and bacon in the pot with the thyme, salt and pepper.
Pour in the stock, cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, until the potato is tender and the sausages cooked through.
Scatter with parsley and serve in bowls with the broth and soda bread.
notes: Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Stovies (Scottish Potato and Corned Beef Hash)
recipes.summary: A frugal Scottish one-pot of soft potatoes, onion and beef dripping or butter, with corned beef.
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pot and cook the onion for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the potato, stock, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Cover and cook gently for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is soft and slightly broken.
Fold in the corned beef and cook for 5 minutes, until hot all the way through.
Serve with oatcakes or beetroot.
notes: Corned beef from a tin is already cooked; just heat it through. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Mince and Tatties (Scottish Beef Mince with Mashed Potato)
recipes.summary: The Scottish weeknight plate: savoury mince with carrot and onion over buttery mash.
steps: Brown the mince in a pan for 8 minutes. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the stock and worcestershire. Simmer for 25 minutes, until thick.
Boil the potato for 18 minutes, until soft. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and salt.
Serve the mince beside the mash.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Roast Beef with Yorkshire Puddings
recipes.summary: Roast sirloin with golden Yorkshire puddings and gravy, the centrepiece of a British Sunday lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Rub the beef with oil, salt and pepper and sit on the onion in a tin. Roast 20 minutes, then reduce to 180°C (160°C fan) and roast 40 to 60 minutes, until 60°C for medium.
Whisk the cup of flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and rest for 30 minutes.
Parboil the potatoes for 10 minutes, then roast them in a second tin with a little oil for 45 minutes, until golden.

Rest the beef for 20 minutes. Raise the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put 1 tsp vegetable oil in each hole of a 12-hole muffin tin and heat for 5 minutes until smoking. Pour in the batter and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and golden. Don't open the oven early.
Whisk 2 tbsp flour into the beef juices, add the stock and simmer 5 minutes. Carve and serve with everything.
notes: Food safety: roast beef is safe at 60°C for medium or 70°C for well done in the centre; rest it before carving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

recipes.title: Roast Chicken with Sage and Onion Stuffing
recipes.summary: A whole roast chicken with a crisp skin and a savoury sage and onion stuffing baked alongside.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Rub the chicken with the softened butter, thyme, salt and pepper and put the lemon inside. Roast for 20 minutes.
Reduce to 190°C (170°C fan) and cook for 1 hour more, until the juices run clear and a thermometer reads 75°C in the thickest part of the thigh.
Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes. Mix with the breadcrumbs, sage and 1/2 cup stock, press into a small dish and bake for the last 25 minutes.
Parboil the potatoes for 10 minutes and roast around the chicken for the last 40 minutes.
Rest the chicken for 15 minutes. Make gravy by whisking the flour and 1 cup stock into the pan juices over heat for 5 minutes.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk. Cook stuffing in a separate dish, not inside the bird.

recipes.title: Linguine allo Scoglio (Rock Pool Seafood Linguine)
recipes.summary: Linguine with mussels, clams, prawns and squid in a garlicky white wine and tomato sauce.
steps: Cook the linguine in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Keep 1 cup of the water.
Soften the garlic and chilli in the oil for 1 minute. Add the wine and tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes, until slightly thick.
Add the mussels and clams, cover and cook for 4 minutes, until they open. Discard any that stay shut.
Add the prawns and squid and cook for 3 minutes, until opaque.
Toss the drained pasta in the pan with a splash of the water for 2 minutes. Scatter with parsley and serve.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish. Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Spaghetti alle Vongole (Spaghetti with Clams)
recipes.summary: A Neapolitan beachside classic of spaghetti, clams, garlic, white wine and parsley.
steps: Cook the spaghetti in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Keep 1/2 cup of the water.
Warm the oil, garlic and chilli for 2 minutes. Add the clams and wine, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the shells open. Discard any that stay shut.
Add the drained spaghetti and a splash of water. Toss over medium heat for 2 minutes, until the sauce clings.
Stir in the parsley and serve.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Bucatini all'Amatriciana (Bucatini with Pork Cheek and Tomato)
recipes.summary: Hollow pasta in a sharp tomato sauce with crisp cured pork and pecorino from Amatrice.
steps: Fry the pancetta in the oil for 8 minutes, until crisp, with the chilli. Add the wine and boil for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Cook the bucatini in salted water until al dente. Drain, saving a splash of water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce for 1 minute with half the pecorino and a splash of water. Serve with the rest of the cheese.
notes: Food safety: cured pork should be cooked until crisp and eaten the same day, or refrigerated within an hour. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pecorino, a hard cheese that usually isn't vegetarian.

recipes.title: Penne all'Arrabbiata (Angry Penne)
recipes.summary: Penne in a fiery garlic and chilli tomato sauce, a Roman plate that takes ten minutes to make.
steps: Warm the oil, garlic and chilli over low heat for 2 minutes, until the garlic is just golden.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and 1 tsp salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Cook the penne in salted water until al dente and drain, saving a splash of water.
Toss the penne through the sauce, add the parsley and a splash of water and serve.
notes: Vegan and dairy-free. Add a little more chilli if you like it hotter.

recipes.title: Boeuf Bourguignon
recipes.summary: Beef braised slowly in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and pearl onions, served with mash.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Fry the bacon in the oil in a casserole for 5 minutes. Lift out. Brown the beef in batches for 10 minutes in total. Lift out.
Cook the carrot and onion for 8 minutes. Stir in the flour and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the wine, stock, garlic, herbs, bacon and beef. Bring to a simmer, cover and braise in the oven for 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is very tender.
Fry the mushrooms and pearl onions in a pan for 8 minutes, until golden. Stir through for the last 15 minutes.
Skim off fat and serve with mashed potato.
notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten. Better made a day ahead.

recipes.title: Blanquette de Poulet (French Chicken in Creamy Lemon Sauce)
recipes.summary: Gently simmered veal in a creamy lemon sauce with mushrooms and pearl onions, finished with a yolk liaison.
steps: Put the veal, studded onion, carrot, bay and stock in a pot. Bring to a simmer, skimming, and cook gently for 30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and tender. Strain, keeping the stock and veal.
Simmer the mushrooms and pearl onions in the stock for 10 minutes, then lift out.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in 3 cups of the stock. Simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Whisk the yolks, cream and lemon juice, stir in a little hot sauce, then return all to the pot off the boil, stirring until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Add the veal, mushrooms and onions, heat gently without boiling, and serve over rice.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink. The egg liaison needs to reach about 75°C but must not boil or it will curdle. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Sole Meunière
recipes.summary: Pan-fried fish fillets in browned butter, lemon and parsley, a French bistro classic.
steps: Dry the fish, season and dust lightly with flour.
Heat half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the fish for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and it flakes. Plate.
Wipe the pan, add the remaining butter and cook for 2 minutes until nutty brown.
Add the lemon juice, parsley and capers, swirl and pour over the fish. Serve with potatoes.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains fish, gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Choucroute Garnie (Alsatian Sauerkraut with Sausages and Pork)
recipes.summary: Sauerkraut simmered with white wine, pork belly and sausages, served with potatoes and mustard.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil in a heavy pot for 5 minutes. Add the sauerkraut, wine, stock and bay.
Add the pork belly, cover and simmer on low for 1 hour.
Add the sausages and simmer for 25 minutes, until cooked through. Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes.
Serve the sauerkraut with the pork, sausages, potatoes and mustard.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Sausages must reach 75°C in the centre. Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Arroz Negro (Spanish Black Squid Ink Rice)
recipes.summary: Short grain rice cooked in squid ink and fish stock with squid and prawns, served with garlic mayo.
steps: Soften the onion, garlic and capsicum in the oil in a wide pan for 8 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the squid and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the rice for 1 minute.
Dissolve the ink in the hot stock, pour in and simmer without stirring for 15 minutes, until the rice is nearly tender.
Add the prawns on top, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until pink. Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with aioli.
notes: Food safety: squid and octopus turn tough if cooked briefly then overcooked; cook until opaque and firm. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish, egg (in aioli). Cool any leftover rice quickly and eat within a day.

recipes.title: Zarzuela de Mariscos (Catalan Seafood Stew)
recipes.summary: A Catalan stew of mixed fish and shellfish in a rich tomato, almond and brandy sauce.
steps: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes. Stir in the paprika for 30 seconds, then add the brandy and boil for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and almonds and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Add the fish and squid and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the mussels and prawns, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the shells open and the prawns turn pink. Discard any shells that stay shut.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish, fish and almonds. Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Rabo de Toro (Andalusian Braised Oxtail)
recipes.summary: Oxtail slowly braised in red wine, vegetables and spices until the meat falls from the bone, a Cordoba classic.
steps: Season the oxtail and brown it in the oil in a heavy casserole in batches for 12 minutes in total. Lift out.
Cook the onion, carrot and garlic for 8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste, paprika and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the wine, boil for 3 minutes, then add the stock, bay and oxtail. Cover and cook at 160°C (140°C fan) for 3 hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Add the potato for the last 40 minutes.
Skim the fat and serve the oxtail with the sauce and potatoes.
notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free. Better made a day ahead; skim the set fat before reheating.

recipes.title: Bacalao al Pil Pil (Basque Salt Cod in Garlic Oil Emulsion)
recipes.summary: Fish gently cooked in garlic-infused olive oil that thickens into a glossy emulsion.

items: 4 firm white fish fillets, skin on

steps: Warm the oil and garlic over low heat for 6 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold. Lift out the garlic and chilli and set aside.
Dry the fish and season. Add skin side down to the warm oil and cook gently for 6 minutes, turning once, until just cooked through. Lift out.
Off the heat, swirl the pan in a circular motion for 5 minutes as the oil cools; the gelatin from the skin makes it thicken into a sauce.
Return the fish, spoon the sauce over and top with garlic and chilli. Serve with potatoes.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Salt cod needs 48 hours soaking; this version uses fresh fish. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Cocido Madrileño (Madrid Chickpea and Meat Stew)
recipes.summary: The classic Madrid cocido of chickpeas, pork, chorizo and vegetables, traditionally served in three courses.
steps: Put the pork, chicken, chorizo, onion and water in a large pot. Bring to a simmer, skim, and cook gently for 1 hour.
Add the chickpeas and carrot and simmer for 30 minutes, then add the potato and cabbage and simmer for 25 minutes more, until all are tender.
Lift out the meats and vegetables and slice. Strain 6 cups of broth into a pan and cook the noodles for 4 minutes.
Serve the broth with noodles first, then the meat, chickpeas and vegetables.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Chicken and sausages must reach 75°C. Canned chickpeas are already cooked.
